subject: Decision Making
title: Simplification
description: A short lesson to help you apply Simplification.

hook.text: A college financial aid form was 108 questions long. Simplifying it to 2 pages increased college enrollment by 8.

buildup.text: Simplification sets up the tradeoffs, the uncertainty, and the decision pressure.

discovery.text: The UK Nudge Unit found that simplifying government letters from jargon to plain language doubled response rates.

twist.text: Tax filing in some countries is pre-filled by the government. Citizens just confirm.

climax.text: Simplification is the most powerful nudge. Remove friction and behavior follows. Add friction and behavior stops.

punchline.text: 108 questions to 2 pages. Simplify the form, change the outcome.

quiz.question: Why is simplification an effective nudge?
options: Reducing friction removes barriers to action—each extra step loses more people
